title: Apple's window to appeal the EU General Court's DMA gatekeeper-designation ruling to the CJEU closes
source: NEWS: MacObserver, 'Apple's EU Gatekeeper Status: The July Ruling and This Month's Appeal Deadline' (macobserver.com/news/apple-eu-gatekeeper-status-july-ruling-appeal-deadline/), published 2026-09-13 and fetched direct 2026-09-17, computes the deadline from the EU's own procedural rule — 'two months and ten days after formal notification of that judgment' — applied to the General Court's 2026-07-08 gatekeeper-designation ruling (curia.europa.eu press release cp260096en.pdf, corroborated by Euronews, Courthouse News, ppc.land and Concurrences, all 2026-07-08/09), landing the window's outer edge at 'around September 18'. The date is a SECONDARY computation, not a Commission or CJEU primary stating the exact deadline, and is hedged as such in its own source ('around') — filed estimate on that basis as well as the standing schema gap (no confirmed-prefix slot for a CJEU procedural deadline). A targeted search on 2026-09-17 found no report of Apple having filed an appeal or announced a decision either way; Apple's spokesperson at the time of the ruling 'would not confirm whether it intends to appeal.'
notes: Discovered during the apple-eu-dma-terms-2026-10-01 2026-09-17 pulse-check adjacency sweep, while confirming that entry's 'overhang not retired' list (the €500M anti-steering fine appeal T-438/25, plus the DMA.100203/100204 interoperability proceedings) was still current. This is a DIFFERENT, THIRD proceeding — the gatekeeper-designation challenge the General Court dismissed on 2026-07-08 — and its own appeal-to-CJEU window is a new dated point none of the three already-tracked matters carry a date for. Low impact: this is a procedural deadline, not a scheduled disclosure or ruling — if Apple appeals, the CJEU appeal itself would run for months with no near-term market read; if it lets the window lapse, that forecloses one (already-lost) line of challenge while the live €500M fine appeal and the interoperability proceedings continue untouched. Filed low/geopolitical on the same footing as this calendar's other litigation-deadline entries (e.g. missouri-map-tro-expiry-2026-09-22). If the lane that researches this id finds Apple has already filed, declined, or that the true deadline differs from this NEWS-sourced computation, the proposal is inert and costs nothing — which is why it is a proposal and not a canonical file.
